problem: Embedded point reads still pay worker delivery and ordinary snapshot/transaction preparation. Does bounded immutable overlay capture suffice to remove those boundaries?
decision: Retain the existing worker/watchdog and shared semantic execution. Preserve the private source experiment and counterexample; integrate documentation only.

alternatives.name: Use bounded overlay capture directly as record.get execution
alternatives.defeated_by: Real reader exhaustion: ordinary published replica construction returns WouldBlock at MAX_READER_PINS; the source-only capture still succeeds. It has no semantic admission, transaction witness reservation, blob codec, response proof or execution watchdog.

alternatives.name: Treat scope and byte ownership tests as complete certification
alternatives.defeated_by: Those tests prove only source lifetime, exact scoped key lookup, health refusal and raw-byte retention; they do not exercise a semantic request or its limits.

alternatives.name: Skip reader capacity and transport isolation for a fast result
alternatives.defeated_by: Changes authority/resource/lifecycle behavior and violates the existing FFI contract.

baseline.scope: Private research only; production and other sessions unchanged.

prototype.runtime_reachability: No callers outside the private tests; no request fast path implemented.

adversarial_initial_compile.reason: Test accessed nonexistent exported reader_handles field; corrected to actual private registry field.

adversarial_final.scope: Private source lease tests only, not a full package/release gate.

demonstrated: Captured old/new values and versions remain distinct across publication; owner 99 cannot read owner 11 key.
Oversize, materialized source, view contention, barrier contention, latched WAL error and restart-required authority decline capture.
After complete merge, pending overlay bytes are zero; retained source bytes remain accounted until the last captured source drops.
A captured tombstone is distinct from a key absent from the overlay.
Real MAX_READER_PINS exhausted reader handles produce WouldBlock on ordinary capture while source-only capture still succeeds.

performance.reason: Admission counterexample defeats production equivalence before any performance comparison. No CPU, latency or SQLite claim follows from avoiding pins.

next_design_requirements: Shared semantic compiler/admission, including task_results handling and exact authenticated scope.
A bounded nonblocking permit with capacity/close/poison/error parity; retaining an Arc accounts bytes but grants no read permit.
Strict inline document decode and exact response proof; blob/tree/error/uncertainty fall back.
Preserve detached worker execution/watchdog, panic/timeout poison behavior and caller-buffer ownership.
Matched frozen source default-off SDK/native CPU/latency/tail comparisons before selection.
